festivals.name: Ganeshotsav (Ganesh Chaturthi)
festivals.description: Pune is world-renowned for its grand 10-day Ganeshotsav celebrations, pioneered by Lokmanya Tilak in 1893. Features the Manache 5 Gananpati processions, rhythmic Dhol-Tasha troupes, and intricate theme pandals.

festivals.name: Palkhi Festival (Wari)
festivals.description: An 800-year-old annual pilgrimage walk where hundreds of thousands of Warkaris walk on foot from Dehu & Alandi to Pandharpur carrying holy footwear (Padukas) of Sant Tukaram and Sant Dnyaneshwar.

cuisines.name: Misal Pav
cuisines.specialty: Spicy sprouted moth bean curry topped with farsan, onions, lemon and served with hot buttery pav.

cuisines.name: Puran Poli
cuisines.specialty: Sweet flatbread stuffed with cooked chana dal, jaggery, cardamom, and served with generous dollops of pure desi ghee.

cuisines.name: Pithla Bhakri & Thecha
cuisines.specialty: Traditional rustic dish of cooked besan curry served with hot Jowar/Bajra Bhakri and fiery green chili-garlic thecha.

crafts.name: Puneri Pagadi
crafts.description: A distinct turban headgear recognized as a symbol of pride, honor, and intellect in Pune since the Peshwa era.

crafts.name: Tambat Metal Craft (Coppersmithing)
crafts.description: Traditional hand-beaten copper and brass utensil craft practiced by the Tambat craft community in Kasba Peth.
